quest.title: The Story Begins in a Forest Without Rain
quest.description: "They will descend upon the 'Cliff of Prophecy'..."
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.num: Summertide Scales and Tales: Page I
chapter.title: The Story Begins in a Forest Without Rain

talks.objective: Open the strange book
Examine the surrounding area

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Wake up! Heyyy~!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, you're finally awake! Paimon was worried sick!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No idea... Paimon just woke up, and then we were here... Paimon's head is all dizzy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #The scenery here looks different, too... *whimper* What should we do, {NICKNAME}? Please don't tell Paimon someone abducted us and brought us to some strange place that we can never leave...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You're right. Better to think of this as... the beginning of a new adventure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew... Thank goodness you're still here. If Paimon woke up alone, she probably would be trembling in a tree hollow...

choices.text: Let's take a look around first...

talks.objective: Continue exploring along the path

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, did those plants by the road look weird to you? It almost looked like... they were made of paper!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And those two frogs over there... Yeah, they look like pieces of origami!
Oh! By the shade of a lotus leaf, Stream, don't tell me you forgot how to jump!

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: I... I didn't forget, Firecracker. I'm just... not sure if what I remember is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: Hah, next thing you know you'll have forgotten how to sing, much less notate a score. You still remember why we call you Stream, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: Yeah, because I've got a great singing voice. Although, these days, the name seems more ironic than anything...

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: Not just a great voice, one that evokes the gentleness of early morning dewdrops flowing into a spring! So, cheer up, and make the jump over! If you're still unsure, just use that roll of magic thread. I won't laugh, I promise. Now, don't tell me you've forgotten how to use that as well...

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: I haven't forgotten everything, Firecracker. Your name, for instance — it's kinda hard to forget that you're named after your fiery temper. Now do me a favor, and pipe down for a second. I'll be right over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You saw that too, right!? Paimon's not seeing things, is she?

choices.text: I saw some talking paper frogs...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This place is getting more confusing by the second...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, uh... Why don't we go after those two frogs? They didn't look evil or anything. Plus, they might be able to help us out!

talks.objective: Follow the Paper Frogs
Follow the Paper Frogs

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: I've placed the bottle where you requested. The rest is up to you, my lady.

talks.objective: Continue forward along the path

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we're not catching up to those frogs... They were so fast, Paimon couldn't even tell where they hopped off to in the end...
Excuse me, honored travelers... Did you come from the Cliff of Prophecy perchance?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh! The... The chubby paper hamster just talked!
Chubby... Who are you calling chubby? I've just got a slightly thicker layer of paper on me, that's all!

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Ahem... Allow me to introduce myself. My name is Almond, and I'm an elder of the Forest of Blessings. I've been waiting here for the Hero of Prophecy to arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... Could you pinch Paimon just to make sure she's not still dreaming?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I need pinching as well...

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Pinching, you say? I can help with that... although you'll have to get a little closer, my arms are rather short.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—That's alright... We just need a minute to collect ourselves. Okay... Let's think things through...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We know for sure this isn't the world we're familiar with. The talking paper animals and all the paper trees and plants make that pretty clear.

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: "The Hero from another world, supported by their companions, shall restore peace to this world..." That is what the prophecy says.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Oh, dearie me — I completely forgot to introduce you to this world, didn't I? And here I am, getting all excited by the arrival of the Hero... You'll have to excuse me, this old brain isn't what it once was... all shell and no nuts.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Perhaps my once-glossy paper has faded past the point of no return...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, really! You can just tell us all about this world now.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Let me think... Where should I even begin? I've pretty much forgotten everything that happened in the past...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Ah, right, I believe the story circulating along the pulp of this forest goes as follows...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: A long, long time ago, three goddesses created this world, and named it "Simulanka."

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: The Goddess of Creation, who presides over matter and magic, created the mountains and rivers, and gave us life. Her powers also paved the way for Simulanka to exist in numerous worlds.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: After the Goddess of Creation came the Goddess of Prophecy, with dominion over the stars and the course of fate itself. She induced the sky to spin, and the earth to move. Even to this day, her statue still stands tall at the highest point of Constellation Metropole.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: The final Goddess was the Goddess of Fate, she who reigns over all treasured tales and dearest wishes. She bestowed upon us the fierce and everlasting feelings of love and hate, and showed us the meaning of death and hope.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, they all seem super impressive! Sounds like they really did a lot.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Of course. All new residents of Simulanka come to the Forest to thank the Goddess of Creation for founding this world, and travel to Constellation Metropole to witness the divinations of the Goddess of Prophecy's numerous oracles.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: After that, they make their way to the end of the world, and tell the Goddess of Fate about their most cherished dreams. *sigh* At least, that's how it used to be.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... "How it used to be"? Did something bad happen?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You mentioned something about "restoring peace to this world"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah! That has to do with the Hero you're waiting for, right?

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Yes... This old brain of mine may have forgotten many things, but I will never forget the day the evil dragon descended upon our Forest...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: It came down from the skies in an ominous black mist and ravaged our homeland... its gigantic footprints can still be seen in the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells. We're incredibly fortunate that no one was hurt...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds terrifying...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: The terror doesn't stop there, I'm afraid... Ever since the attack, the Calligraphy Tavern in the forest has been closed. No one knows why, but it is a catastrophe of the highest order for us forest-dwellers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? A catastrophe of the highest order... all because a Tavern closed? If we were talking about Mondstadt, here, Paimon might understand, but is it really all that serious?

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Good Goddess of Creation above, we'd take even the greatest flood over the closure of the Tavern!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Wet paper will dry out with time, fallen trees can be restored... But the Calligraphy Tavern is the only source of the <color=#00E1FFFF>Magic Tonic</color> that sustains all creatures in the forest!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Magic... what?

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Magic Tonic. It was gifted to the forest by the Goddess of Creation herself — a special potion that helps us maintain our vitality.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What happens if you stop drinking it?

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Well... Our bodies will gradually crumple and become brittle, until they eventually disintegrate entirely. Our <color=#00E1FFFF>colors will fade</color>, and we'll start to lose our memory, until we can't even remember our own names...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? But wait, Grandpa Almond, does that mean you've already...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: I'm afraid so... The color has all but completely faded from my paper. To be honest, all I really remember is that I'm supposed to wait here for the Hero of Prophecy. But, I've already forgotten who gave me that order to begin with...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, we've got to act fast! How can we help?

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Oh, brave pixie, may the Goddess of Fate reward you and your friend for your kindness.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Could it be... you're the Heroes I've been waiting for all along?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Not sure how we'd know that. Plus, we can't even remember how we got here. So, it's not looking too promising...

choices.text: We were just following the road, and then ended up here...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Well... this is turning out to be quite the conundrum for old almond-brain here. The prophecy never mentioned anything like that...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: For now, why don't you come with me to the Hut of Blessings? Our Forest Fairy lives there. Maybe she'll know what to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, a Forest Fairy? Like, one that knows magic?

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Oh, you betcha. She's prophesized to join the Hero on their journey.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well then, she sounds like exactly the kind of person we need! Please lead the way, Grandpa Almond!

choices.text: We're trying to find a way back to our world...

dialogues.speaker: Citrus
dialogues.text: What flavor of Magic Tonic should I whip up first?

talks.objective: Go to the Hut of Blessings

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: This is the place. If you could just wait a moment, the Fairy should be—
#...! {NICKNAME}, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon knows that voice...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: ...It's really you! I'm so happy to see you!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Ah! Sorry, sorry...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Nilou is the Forest Fairy? Well, you certainly look the part!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hehe, thank you! But to be honest, I'm still getting used to it...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: It's the weirdest thing. I remember I was reading a book at the Grand Bazaar, and then I guess I must have fallen asleep at some point, because... well, then I woke up dressed like this...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: And, in my dream, someone spoke to me. They said: "You are the Fairy of the Forest of Blessings. Now go, save the forest with your magic."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: At first, I thought this whole world was just part of the dream, but no matter how hard I tried, I couldn't seem to wake up. I couldn't find anyone I knew from the real world, either...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds similar to what happened with us! We also have no idea how we got here...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Anyway, sorry for my reaction back there... I got a bit too excited when I saw you two...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, we totally understand! We were looking for a way out, too. At least we know we're not alone!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Oh, blessed be the Goddess of Fate above, you're already friends with the Fairy of the Forest!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Grandpa Almond, thank you so much for bringing my friends here. Could you let the others know I'm coming? I'll head over right away.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Of course, leave it to me!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Hey-ho, pistachio! Today truly is a blessed day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Nilou, looks like you made short work of getting to know the locals!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Well... when I arrived here yesterday, Grandpa Almond told me all about the state of this world. Since they think of me as their Forest Fairy, I just felt like I had to try to help them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh! So, you mean like... using some kind of Forest magic to repair the Tavern?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Unfortunately, I don't know how to use the "magic" of this world. I've tried using my Vision, but it doesn't seem to work here...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: If the books stored in this hut are anything to go by, this seems to be the place where the Goddess of Creation first made the townspeople of this Forest.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: She folded the pages of books into small origami animals, gave them life with her magic, and with time, that's how the Forest of Blessings took shape.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Maybe one of the books here could teach us how to use magic?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I read them all, but only found one reference to magic—

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: "The incantation, 'Abracadabra,' means 'to create what I say.' This is a world made of words, where fantastical powers can be wielded by all."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okaayy... So, basically, everyone in this world can use magic? That's nice, but still kinda vague...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yeah, from the other books I read, it seems like this goddess really likes to play fast and loose with the details.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... what should we do now? Um, didn't you say you were going somewhere, Nilou?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Oh, yes. I was going to help some of the other residents of the Forest. They've been busy making preparations to reopen the Tavern, so I thought I could help out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it! Guess we should just focus on what we can do for now.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: This whole thing is making me pretty nervous, actually... It's like I've been pushed on stage without being taught the choreography!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Since I'm already wearing the costume, though, I might as well try to play the part. It's what a professional dancer would do.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: And, who knows, maybe I'll find my own magic along the way! All I can do is try, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: At least you're optimistic!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll be there to cheer you on, too.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Thank you! Then, let's go.

choices.text: Maybe... calm down a bit first...

dialogues.speaker: Chestnut
dialogues.text: Look, the Forest Fairy is here! And she brought her companions! Grandpa Almond was right, they do look promising!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hello there, everyone. I heard you were working on the piping for the Calligraphy Tavern. Is there anything we can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Chestnut
dialogues.text: Ah, we wouldn't dream of troubling you with our petty problems, my lady! Don't you worry, we have it all under control.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure about that? Because from where Paimon's floating, the piping is looking pretty chaotic...

dialogues.speaker: Chestnut
dialogues.text: Ah, yes... we have my careless friend to thank for that. He promised we could leave the pipe-connecting to him, and... well, the results speak for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Ginkgo
dialogues.text: Hey...! I just wanted to inspect each pipe! This is the network the Magic Tonic has to flow through. I was just trying to be thorough! So, I... I disassembled the whole thing...

dialogues.speaker: Chestnut
dialogues.text: Yeah, and now you've forgotten how to put the thing back together! *sigh* Have you been eating too many nuts again? 'Cause you are what you eat...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Please, don't fight. I know everyone wants the Tavern to reopen as soon as possible so that the Forest can return to normal.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: So, why don't you let us help out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we're here anyway, so we might as well be helpful! We just need to reassemble these pipes, right?

dialogues.speaker: Chestnut
dialogues.text: Well, if you're offering... Basically, the pipes need to be connected properly to allow the Magic Tonic to <color=#00E1FFFF>flow through</color>. If you put the wrong pipe in the wrong place, the Tonic will get stuck halfway...

dialogues.speaker: Ginkgo
dialogues.text: Attention to detail is key.

dialogues.speaker: Chestnut
dialogues.text: Says the guy who messed the whole thing up in the first place!

dialogues.speaker: Ginkgo
dialogues.text: Amazing! You did it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now, the Tonic will flow into everyone's cups without getting stuck, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gotta say, though, Paimon is starting to get pretty curious about this Magic Tonic... Um, could she have a teeny tiny sip? Just a little taste! Please!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's not greed! It's curiosity!

response.speaker: Chestnut
response.text: Well... if it's really just one sip, I guess that would be fine...

response.speaker: Ginkgo
response.text: Just... Be careful! This is one of the last cups left in the entire Forest! We're supposed to save it for our research!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just a sip, promise! Okay, here goes... Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Ugh! What was that? It's sticking to Paimon's tongue! Wait, is this just regular <color=#00E1FFFF>ink</color>?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Ink" and "paper," huh...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Wait, does that mean... What the legend says is true?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: "The Goddess of Fate used ink to compose her stories on paper, and the Goddess of Creation used her power to bring those tales to life."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder the Tavern is so important to the Forest...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Maybe the Fading Disorder occurs when the ink within the body dries up... That would explain why the beings here are forgetting their own stories...

response.speaker: Chestnut
response.text: I'm not sure I can really wrap my head around this conversation, but there's no need to get all worked up on our behalf, my lady. With the pipe installed, I'm sure the Tavern will be up and running in no time.

response.speaker: Ginkgo
response.text: What do you mean, can't wrap your head around it? The Fairy is recounting the story of how the Goddesses gave us life. In fact, I've seen the Goddess of Creation with my own eyes!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Really?

response.speaker: Chestnut
response.text: Don't be ridiculous, there's no way you're old enough to have met her! We're the same age — and I think I would know, considering we went to tell our wishes to the Goddess of Fate together! So stop talking a load of paper mache.

response.speaker: Ginkgo
response.text: Fine... It was my grandfather, alright? He was the one that saw her.

response.speaker: Ginkgo
response.text: He said that one day, after he finished work, he saw the Goddess of Creation grant us life with his own eyes.

response.speaker: Ginkgo
response.text: In her hands, she held the very paper used to form our bodies. She whispered something into the pages... And then, suddenly, a paper frog was born, ready to leap into the world! Oh, it was spectacular!

response.speaker: Chestnut
response.text: Cut the theatrics, will you? You weren't even there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so... That's it? Paimon thought creation magic would have a little bit more... pizzazz.

response.speaker: Ginkgo
response.text: Oh! So, in your world, the creation of life is a much showier affair? I'm learning something new every day!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Well, that's not exactly what Paimon was trying to say...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Magic... doesn't have to be spectacular...

response.speaker: Chestnut
response.text: That's enough out of you. All your boasting is confusing our kind Fairy!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Oh, no, it's alright. I actually think I understand the magic of this world a bit better now. Thank you.

response.speaker: Ginkgo
response.text: The honor was all ours, my lady.

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: Stream! Your rhythm is off again! At this rate, it doesn't even matter if the Tavern reopens. The band's not going to even get any gigs.

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I'm sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Uh, hello there... I hope we aren't interrupting your rehearsal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, these are the two frogs we saw on the road a little while ago!

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: Ah, the Forest Fairy is here! For the love of lotus leaves and dewdrops, Stream, you've really gotta put in some effort now!

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: But... I...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, don't pressure yourselves on my account! Are you rehearsing for a show?

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: Sure are! You see, our group regularly performs for guests at the Tavern.

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: We've been out of work for quite some time, with the closure and all. But, after hearing of the Fairy's arrival yesterday, we figured we needed to get in performance shape right away!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hehe, I understand how you feel! Back at the Grand Bazaar, Zubayr Theater's always busy with rehearsals too.

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: The Grand Bazaar? Do people there sing on lotus leaves as well?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Yeah, they do, and it's a reaaaaaally big one! You're the conductor of your group, aren't you? You remind me of Mr. Zubayr!

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: Ah, then he must be an ambitious director, one who would do anything to avoid disappointing a single member of the audience. It's just...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Is there anything we can do to help you, Mr. Stream?

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: Oh, no, no, my problems are... mine and mine alone...

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: It's just... after the Tavern closed, I somehow forgot how to sing... I'm always a few beats behind everyone else, and I keep singing out of key...

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: You were our trump card, our best singer by a mile...

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: I know, I know... But... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he is a victim of the Fading Disorder, too...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Don't be sad, Mr. Stream! Whenever I've forgotten important dance steps in the past, my friends at the Grand Bazaar always stick by my side to encourage me!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: They smile, and patiently tell me everything's going to be okay. Then they play the melody for me over and over, until the steps finally come back to me... Now, it's our turn to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We just need to help you remember how to sing, right? {NICKNAME}'s got a great sense of rhythm. We can help keep you in time!

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: Well, what do you say, Stream? I think it's a great idea. Just focus on the lyrics, and the Fairy's friends will help you stay on beat.

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: Are... Are you sure? This is... really asking a lot...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it, Mr. Stream. It'll all be worth it when the Tavern reopens and we finally have the chance to hear your marvelous singing voice.

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: Alright then... Thank you so much, everyone. I—I'll give it my best shot!

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: Still no good...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, don't give up just yet! Our rhythm was probably off. Let's give it a few more tries!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure, it's good to take a breather. We can come back to this later!

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: I feel like... I'm getting the hang of it again!

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: Goddesses above, this better stick when it comes to the performance! Just do it exactly like how we rehearsed!

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone... Thanks to you, my voice is once again as clear as a flowing stream!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Glad to hear that you're feeling better, Mr. Stream. It's also about time for us to go to our next destination.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mhm! We'll be looking forward to your performance at the Tavern!

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: My dear Citrus, please tell me you're joking. We can't have you out of commission with the Tavern about to reopen!

dialogues.speaker: Citrus
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Grandpa Almond, it's the truth. I was just too excited for the reopening, and must've fallen asleep in an awkward position.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grandpa Almond! We're here to help!

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Oh, hazelnuts on high, you could not have come at a better time! Please, allow me to introduce you. This is the bartender of the Calligraphy Tavern, Miss Citrus.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She's so tall...

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Miss Citrus is supposed to add all kinds of delicious fruits to the Magic Tonic. Her additions are what turn it into the finest brew in the land. She's indispensable to the operation of the Tavern!

dialogues.speaker: Citrus
dialogues.text: I appreciate the kind words, Grandpa Almond, but... Owww... My neck...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Citrus
dialogues.text: Ah, terrible timing... getting a kink in my neck at a time like this...

dialogues.speaker: Citrus
dialogues.text: Could you give my tail a little twist? That should help free up the movement in my neck. I would do it myself, but I can't reach on my own, and Grandpa Almond is too old, and as light as a feather...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The neck and tail... are connected?

dialogues.speaker: Citrus
dialogues.text: Of course they're connected! Just like how you can't have a rainbow without rain. Anyway, you just need to position me <color=#00E1FFFF>at the right height</color> to pick the fruits, and then put them <color=#00E1FFFF>in the barrel over there</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Citrus
dialogues.text: Perfect! My neck feels much better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So there really is some kind of connection between your neck and tail...

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, everyone! I can rest easy now, knowing the drinks at the Tavern will be just as wonderful as before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's another problem solved!

talks.objective: Help the forest dwellers with Nilou

dialogues.speaker: Ginkgo
dialogues.text: ...See, I was right! That's exactly what the Goddess of Creation did all those years ago!

dialogues.speaker: Chestnut
dialogues.text: Ugh, brag away. But, don't think you're getting out of carrying all those pipes with me later.

talks.objective: Help the forest dwellers with Nilou

dialogues.speaker: Firecracker
dialogues.text: For the sake of the Forest Fairy, Stream, please give me your best performance when we take the stage!

dialogues.speaker: Stream
dialogues.text: Rest easy, Firecracker. I've been waiting for this day for a very long time.

talks.objective: Help the forest dwellers with Nilou

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Forest... Please heed my words, and accept my blessings...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: May your spring of wondrous magic never run dry, and may all who call you their home lead happy, fulfilling lives...

talks.objective: Return to the Hut of Blessings

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, since we've taken care of most of the tasks, all we need to do now is reopen the Tavern!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: But, we still don't know how to use the magic of this world. We don't even know why the Tavern closed in the first place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Oh! What about the method that one hamster mentioned? You should try it, Nilou!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You mean, the creation magic his grandfather saw outside the Hut of Blessings? Hmm, I wonder... How exactly did the Goddess of Creation give them life...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe... you don't need to understand it, just give it a try! Everyone here calls you the Forest Fairy. Maybe you have the magic powers already, and you just don't know it!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: In other words... this Forest is a stage, and all I need to do is... step out into the spotlight? Hehe, sounds just like a fairytale!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we are surrounded by talking origami animals and magic potions, after all... Almost seems like anything's possible in this place.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You're right, Paimon. We won't know anything unless we try. In that case... Let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nilou takes out a page from a book, and folds it into the shape of a hamster...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: This is how you do it, right? I think I got the folds right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Your origami skills are great!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I once saw one of our prop people make something similar. It looked really cool, so I took some time during my break to learn the basics. It's not a bad way to stave off sleepiness, either!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, how do you feel? Sense any... uhh... magical powers flowing through you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No? Hmm... What are we missing?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aren't you supposed to say some magic words?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Magic words? But, how am I supposed to know what the Goddess said to bring them to life?

choices.text: It doesn't matter what she said...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, good point! You're the Forest Fairy, Nilou, what do you want to say to the new resident of your domain?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Nilou picks up the hamster, and kisses it gently on the forehead...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: "I bestow upon you the blessings of the forest, and offer you a home in this land..."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: "Your name shall be Padisarah. May you bloom in this world as beautifully as the flower I love."

response.speaker: Padisarah
response.text: My name is... Padisarah.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It worked! It actually worked!!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Well, peel my shell and call me a nut... I never imagined I'd witness such a miracle at my age. It's just like what the stories said about the Goddess of Creation!

response.speaker: Padisarah
response.text: Shell... miracle...?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Nice to meet you, Padisarah. I'm Nilou, the Fairy of this Forest. From this day forward, this place is now your home.

response.speaker: Padisarah
response.text: Hello, Fairy Nilou!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I hope you'll grow up happily in this Forest.

response.speaker: Padisarah
response.text: Grow up...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Hahaha, you can leave the little one with old Almond for now. Oho, this sure brings back memories... It's been such a long time since we last held a welcome ceremony.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Here, Padisarah. Come to Grandpa Almond.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, now that Nilou has mastered the Goddess' magic, we should be able to reopen the Tavern, right?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hmm... Grandpa Almond, could you send a few people to check the underground space beneath the Tavern?

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Oh, of course! May I ask why?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: The moment I used magic, I sensed something... strange down there. I have a feeling it's connected to why the Tavern had to close down.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Of course, we'll look into it right away.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Make sure you listen to Grandpa Almond, Padisarah. Don't go running off on your own!

response.speaker: Padisarah
response.text: Padisarah... listen... running!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Hey, come back here, you! Wait!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, that's Nilou's creation all right. She's got so much energy... Anyway, how did you manage it, Nilou?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Well... All I did was say my wishes for her out loud. Maybe the magic is in the words, themselves, just like the book said!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This place is seeming more like a fairytale by the second.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I mean... we're somewhere called the Forest of Blessings, so it kind of makes sense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, anyway, Paimon thinks this magic suits you perfectly, Nilou!

choices.text: What about the space under the Tavern...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: ...When I brought Padisarah to life just now, I was able to sense the magic flowing through the Forest — in the flowers and trees, and inside the creatures that live here...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: But for some reason, there's a hollowed-out space beneath the Tavern where I couldn't sense anything at all...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: We're back, my lady!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was fast!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: You were right, there was something under the Tavern that I've never seen before! It looked transparent, and gave off a... clinking sound when I knocked on it.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Transparent and clinking... Oh! I've got it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, already!?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Haha, you've got to use fairytale logic, Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Is it an "ink bottle"?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: That's right! <color=#00E1FFFF>An empty ink bottle</color>, to be exact. Still remember the taste of the "Magic Tonic" you took a sip of, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it was... ink! Oh, Paimon gets it now.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: You've lost old nuts-for-brains again, I'm afraid... But, no matter, is there anything else we can do to help?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, will you come gather some ingredients with me? I learned what we need to make the Magic Tonic back in the Hut of Blessings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing! What do we need to get?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hmmm... "A setting sun that never sets," "a dragon that cannot fly," and "a moon that only shines at night."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Where are we supposed to find crazy things like that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She means sunsettias, snapdragons, and Nilotpala Lotuses.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? How did you get that so fast?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Fairytale logic," Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Logic, huh? Lucky guess, more like...

choices.text: Focus on what you want to say.

talks.objective: Collect the materials used to make Magic Tonic
Collect the materials used to make Magic Tonic
Collect the materials used to make Magic Tonic
Collect the materials used to make Magic Tonic
Return to the Hut of Blessings

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Give me just a second. I'm gonna go fetch an ink bottle from the other room.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get it... All the ingredients are super tasty, but, somehow, the final product turns into ink...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, anyway, Paimon's not going anywhere near the stuff this time, not even if you bribed her...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Sorry to keep you waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Let's see... According to the book, first you do this... then this... and then...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: ...It's done!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, magic sure makes everything super convenient!

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Yes, this is it... This is exactly the Magic Tonic we need!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Grandpa Almond, could you take the concoction to the room underneath the Tavern and place it next to the transparent bottle you found? I'll handle the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Of course! As you command, so it shall be done!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Phew... I still get nervous at times like this. It's just like when you step on stage, and you can tell that every single person's gaze is fixed right on you.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hehe, thanks, you two! I can't tell you how great it is to have you by my side. Almost makes me feel like I've been blessed by the Goddess of Fate, too!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Let's go. We shouldn't keep everyone waiting.

talks.objective: Give the Magic Tonic to Grandpa Almond
Give the Magic Tonic to Grandpa Almond
Go to the Calligraphy Tavern
Talk to everyone

dialogues.speaker: Padisarah
dialogues.text: Fairy Nilou is amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's so pretty! What a beautiful Tavern!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: It matches the scenery of the Forest perfectly. I was so surprised when it suddenly opened up like that... Just like a pop-up book!

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: ...I remember now. I remember everything!

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: ...It was me. I was the one who went to the top of <color=#00E1FFFF>Constellation Metropole</color>, and witnessed the Goddess's prophecy!

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: "The Hero who shall save this world will descend upon the Cliff of Prophecy. The Hero, supported by their companions, shall restore peace to this world."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the prophecy really did have all the answers, you just forgot the first half...

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: That's why I was waiting near the Cliff of Prophecy... Haha, wonderful, simply wonderful! There's still some hope left for old Almond after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is the Cliff of Prophecy that place with the huge mural? 'Cause that is where we woke up, but we don't remember anything about how we got there. Also, we didn't get a change of clothes like Nilou... Are we definitely the Heroes?

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: If not you, then who else? You've already helped the Fairy revitalize our Forest. To us, that makes you heroes, prophesized or not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Either way, we're going to keep adventuring, even if just to figure out how we can get back to our world.

choices.text: We can also help resolve any crises along the way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, that's exactly right! Helping people we meet on the road is kind of our thing!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: As expected, the words of the Goddess of Prophecy always come true.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I'll come with you. It can't hurt to have a magical Fairy tag along, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heroes and fairies, dragons and new adventures... Heh, this is sounding more and more like a fairytale by the second!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Hmm, I would say your next stop should be Constellation Metropole. It's Simulanka's most prosperous city, just across the sea.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Once you've arrived at the Astral Garden at the highest point in the city, maybe you can try seeking divine counsel from the Goddess of Prophecy herself.

response.speaker: Padisarah
response.text: ...Are you leaving, Fairy Nilou?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I'm afraid so. There are still other people who need my help. I won't go far, though, and I'll come back to visit the minute I have time to spare.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: So, be a good girl, Padisarah, and help out Grandpa Almond whenever you can, alright?

response.speaker: Padisarah
response.text: Mhm! Got it! Padisarah will wait here for you!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Hahaha, that's a good girl, Padisarah. Ah, I almost forgot — if Constellation Metropole is where you're heading, you'll need to take the Maritime Express.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: I'll head to the station first thing tomorrow morning and wake up that lazy station master for you. Why don't you take a break for the rest of the day? You should savor the beautiful scenery of the Forest before you go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds great! Paimon definitely feels tired after being on the go for so long. There's a spot in the Tavern with Paimon's name on it!

response.speaker: Citrus
response.text: Oh? Sounds like someone is ready to order!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh, well, if you're offering... Paimon will take a glass of Bulle Fruit Tonic! ...Um, but hold the Tonic, hehe!

choices.text: It would be our honor, my lady.
We can also help resolve your dragon problem along the way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! We've beaten up plenty of dragons already, so what's one more?

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Seems like we were just sent a strange book. It does have a really nice cover, though...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's really curious... Let's read it and see what it's about!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... That meadow over there looks pretty strange.

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: That's what the Calligraphy Tavern looks like, now it's lost all of its color...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we should make our way to the next location.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: We've got one final stop. Let's go.
